account: Today seems mostly routine, but there may be an unusual effort to coordinate grain and bread supplies. The secretary told me she overheard the builder discussing a grain shortage and seeking the miller's help, mentioning forty-six hay bales. Neither she nor I has verified that quantity or what it means. The neighbour has now told me she personally saw the baker give bread to the innkeeper yesterday; the innkeeper asked about spare wheat or hay, and freight told her they were seeking the miller about arrangements. She called at the mill this morning but received no answer. These reports suggest people may be arranging grain supplies to keep bread available, though I do not yet know whether there is a real shortage, whose stocks are involved, or the purpose of the forty-six bales. The neighbour also reports the baker said yesterday's bread arrangements went smoothly and fresh baking is underway today. I will ask the miller directly at my scheduled ten o'clock grain inspection rather than treat hearsay as established fact. Separately, the builder has installed eight lanterns in the great hall and will meet me for the confirmed eighteen o'clock lighting inspection. He explicitly said he has no bridge or port works proposed, and I have no verified evidence of such plans. My remaining appointments are lunch at home at noon, council letters at thirteen, tea at the neighbour's dockside cottage at fifteen, office at sixteen-thirty, the lighting inspection at eighteen, and home at nineteen.
